result.summary:
Completed WF-02 Step 2 for REQ-036 (pending-request urgency flag at T-48h and honest auto-decline at registration close). A previous BACKEND-DEV dispatch had already committed the full implementation (commit 188038e) but stalled reporting back while waiting on its own background vitest verification. This pass inspected and verified the committed diff in full against the approved design (docs/agents/design/REQ-036.md) rather than re-implementing: apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts (isRequestUrgent, mirrors isAutoPromotionHalted's exact shape at a 48h threshold), apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts (two new NotificationKind literals: pending_request_urgent, registration_auto_declined), apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts (getPrimaryOrganizerIdForChapter -- ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT 1, deterministic, returns null when no organizer assigned; autoDeclineRequest -- a NEW writer, not a call to rejectRequest, since rejectRequest's signature takes a non-nullable organizerUserId and unconditionally writes a mandatory reason; reuses decideRejectionOutcome completely unchanged; actorUserId: null; new audit action registration.auto_decline; per-candidate db.transaction matching approveRequest/rejectRequest's own commit-then-notify-outside-transaction pattern; isUrgent field added to PendingRequestListItem, computed fresh on every render via isRequestUrgent, never dependent on whether the push notification was ever sent), apps/bot/src/handlers/organizerRequests.ts (urgency marker prefixed onto list rows and the detail view header when isUrgent is true; listPendingRequestsForOrganizer/getPendingRequestForOrganizer widened with an explicit evaluationTime parameter, decisions/0006 compliant -- callers pass new Date() at the handler boundary, never inside a predicate), apps/bot/src/scheduler/urgencyJobs.ts (new -- the T-48h job, framework-free, selectRegistrationsForUrgencyNotice with the same JS-computed-bound-vs-timestamp-column convention domain/reminders.ts already establishes, sends to exactly ONE organizer per candidate via getPrimaryOrganizerIdForChapter, skips entirely with no ledger row when no organizer exists), apps/bot/src/scheduler/autoDeclineJobs.ts (new -- the registration-close job, selectRegistrationsForAutoDecline implements the registrationClosesAt-OR-endsAt-fallback selection exactly as designed, with the catch-up window's 'relevant close instant' correctly computed per-row in JS since Drizzle has no CASE-based column selection this codebase already uses; the job loop moves to the next candidate with zero notification call when outcome.kind !== 'reject', meaning Mechanism 2 (state guard) alone -- with no ledger row ever written -- already prevents a second transition on job restart), apps/bot/src/i18n/{types,en,ru}.ts (urgentMarker, urgentNotification under organizerRequests; a new top-level autoDecline.notification key -- wording is plain, factual, and explicitly does NOT imply personal judgment: 'Nobody reviewed and declined it -- the window simply closed before a decision was made'), apps/bot/src/index.ts (both jobs wired into startScheduledJobs' job list), and apps/bot/src/domain/registrationApproval.db.test.ts (REQ-035's own test file, updated for the two call sites' new evaluationTime parameter -- verified this is a required, not incidental, change: the two functions' signatures genuinely widened, so REQ-035's existing callers needed the same update BACKEND-DEV made everywhere else).

Wording provisional-pending-product-owner disclosure (REQ-014/032 precedent): the auto-decline notification text and the urgency marker/notification text are both placeholder copy; final wording is owned by the product owner, not this pipeline. Exact English strings for the record: urgentMarker '[Urgent] '; urgentNotification 'A request for {event} is still pending 48 hours before it starts. Review it with /requests.'; autoDecline.notification 'Your request for {event} was not decided before registration closed, so it could not be approved. Nobody reviewed and declined it -- the window simply closed before a decision was made.' Russian parallels present in ru.ts, verified for key parity against en.ts/types.ts.

Verification: npm run lint -w apps/bot -- clean, zero errors. npm run build -w apps/bot -- clean tsc build, zero errors. Individual spot-checked test files (withdraw.test.ts, registration.db.test.ts's own AC6 REQ-034 cases traced by reading, not running in isolation due to the issue below) read correctly against the new code paths.

UNRESOLVED, FLAGGED EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN SILENTLY WORKED AROUND: `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` from the repo root could not be gotten to a clean full-suite pass in this session despite four consecutive attempts (including one after `docker restart bot-postgres-1`) -- each attempt failed a different, large, and non-overlapping subset of otherwise-unrelated test files (16 to 23 of 39 files, ranging 70 to 151 of 358 individual tests) with foreign-key-violation errors (e.g. 'Key (chapter_id)=(...) is not present in table "chapters"') that are symptomatic of one test file's shared-fixture TRUNCATE racing another file's still-in-flight seed, NOT of any logic this diff introduces -- the specific failing file set changed between attempts, the failures span files this diff never touches (e.g. withdraw.test.ts, checkinQr.forgery.test.ts, walkin.db.test.ts), and re-running a single failing file in total isolation (`npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.test.ts`) passed cleanly (6/6) every time. This matches this codebase's own documented test-infrastructure flakiness class (ISS-0014's file-parallelism deadlock finding, ISS-0027's identical FK-violation/deadlock signature under plain `npm test`) but is notably worse here than previously observed even WITH the --no-file-parallelism flag applied -- vitest's own startup banner shows '39 workers spawned' despite that flag, meaning per-file process isolation still occurs and a shared module-level DB pool or the scratch Postgres instance's own connection/lock accounting may be contended across those workers in a way `--no-file-parallelism` (which only orders file scheduling, not necessarily worker concurrency) does not fully prevent. This is being surfaced to REVIEWER/TEST-RUNNER for a decision on whether this needs escalation as a new, more severe ISS-00xx entry (the fluctuating failing-file-set and worse-than-prior-runs severity are new information beyond what ISS-0014/ISS-0027 already describe) rather than re-litigated or silently patched around by this step.
issues: PROVISIONAL WORDING (per REQ-014/032 precedent): urgentMarker, urgentNotification, and autoDecline.notification are all placeholder copy pending product-owner review -- see summary for exact strings.

Full-suite `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` could not be verified clean in this session across 4 attempts (including a Postgres container restart) -- each attempt fails a different large subset of unrelated test files with chapter/actor FK violations; every individually-isolated file re-run passes cleanly. This is worse than, but consistent with the failure class of, ISS-0014 and ISS-0027. Recommend REVIEWER/TEST-RUNNER investigate whether this needs its own ISS-00xx entry before this run's Step 4 test verification is attempted, since a Step 4 run may hit the same non-deterministic full-suite failures for reasons unrelated to REQ-036's own test coverage.
